stem: Alok starts with a square. He may build a new square on a diagonal of the given square, or join the midpoints of the given square's sides to form a new square.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names the construction that doubles the area of the given square?

options.text: Building a new square on a diagonal of the given square doubles its area.
Joining the midpoints of the given square's sides doubles its area.
Either construction doubles the area of the given square.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A square on the diagonal has twice the area of the given square. The midpoint square has half the area, so it does not double the area.

teacher.key_rationale: Diagonal construction doubles area; midpoint-inscribed square halves it. Choosing midpoints for double, or treating both as doubling, reverses or confuses those facts.
